record.original_question: Let p be a degree-n polynomial satisfying p(0)=0 and p'(0)≠0, and let μ_j be the roots of p'. Must at least one critical point μ_j satisfy |p(μ_j)/μ_j| ≤ |p'(0)|?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ be a polynomial of degree $n\ge 2$ satisfying $p(0)=0$ and $p'(0)\ne 0$. Let $\mu_1,\mu_2,\ldots,\mu_{n-1}$ denote the (not necessarily distinct) roots of the derivative $p'$, i.e., the critical points of $p$. Prove or disprove: there exists at least one index $j\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$ such that
$$\left|\frac{p(\mu_j)}{\mu_j}\right| \;\le\; |p'(0)|.$$
artifact.status_search_result: Smale's mean value conjecture, posed in 1981, asks whether some critical point μ_j of a polynomial p with p(0)=0 satisfies |p(μ_j)/μ_j| ≤ |p'(0)| (the standard form has constant 1, sometimes stated with constant (n-1)/n). It is known to hold for low degrees (n ≤ 4, with n=5 settled more recently) and partial bounds are known, but the full conjecture remains open as of recent literature (2024).

status_evidence.title: Smale's Mean Value Conjecture and Related Problems (Ng)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing the conjecture and partial progress.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture remains an active open problem with only partial progress since 1981.

status_evidence.title: The domains where Smale's mean value problem does not hold
status_evidence.snippet: 2024 paper examining domains relevant to the conjecture, aiming to settle it.
status_evidence.claim: Recent 2024 work still treats Smale's mean value conjecture as unresolved in general.

status_evidence.title: A bound for Smale's mean value conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Provides a bound towards the conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial bounds are known toward the conjectured constant.
